items.title: Costco Q4 Earnings & Retail Earnings Week
points: Costco reports earnings Thursday, the week's most closely watched release, with deferred revenue (payments received for goods/services not yet delivered) expanding and membership trends under scrutiny.
Analysts see potential valuation re-rating for Costco stock.
Darden Restaurants, Cintas, Paychex, and General Mills also report this week, offering insight into consumer spending and business services demand.
Broader earnings season will reveal corporate pricing power and cost pressures across consumer and business services sectors.

items.title: Trump-Xi Meeting and Geopolitical Risk
points: President Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping Thursday at the White House to discuss trade, tariffs, Taiwan, and AI.
Investors are watching for potential Chinese purchases of Boeing aircraft as a signal of trade tension easing or escalation.
Light U.S. economic data this week shifts investor focus to geopolitical outcomes and corporate guidance; markets bracing for volatility.

items.title: Oracle's AI Spending Defense
points: Oracle's Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO — contracted revenue to be recognized in future periods) increased, with deferred revenue growing 130% and revenue accelerating to 30% year-over-year.
An analyst argues concerns over Oracle's debt and AI capital spending are overstated given the company's history of adapting to major technology shifts.
Stock rated Accumulate in the $134–$198 range, with a 2026 price target of $250 at roughly 7x trailing revenue.

items.title: Meta Connect & Other Major Events
points: Meta's two-day Connect event begins Wednesday, featuring updates on AI, AI-powered glasses, and virtual/mixed reality products.

McDonald's holds an investor day Wednesday; Treasury announces a bond-buyback plan and global PMI (Purchasing Managers' Index, a gauge of manufacturing/services activity) reports are due the same day.
McDonald's and Meta results will shape views on advertising market strength and tech capital expenditure trends.

items.title: Other Notable Items
points: Paramount Skydance plans to leave California.
Chevron and oil executives warn a global fuel crisis has arrived.
Warren Buffett is stepping down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman.
Trump reportedly out-traded all members of Congress combined in recent trades.

items.title: Salesforce's AI Monetization Strategy
points: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says operating unit leaders changed how they run their businesses within 90 days of rolling out new AI technology.
Customers are seeing value delivered almost instantly rather than over multi-year implementation timelines.
Wall Street views this as a potential breakthrough for Salesforce to finally monetize AI effectively, which could drive stock price appreciation.

items.title: Healthcare Cost-Control Shift Toward Employee Choice
points: Oscar Health CEO Mark Bertolini predicts employers will shift to a defined contribution healthcare model, giving employees a fixed budget to buy their own plans instead of employers managing risk directly.
This mirrors the 1980s shift from pension plans to defined contribution retirement plans and echoes the original 2013 promise of the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare).
94% of all employers and 72% of very large employers are considering this approach, with early adoption already seen among small groups (under 100 employees) and mid-market companies.

items.title: Maye Musk Interview
points: Maye Musk, mother of Elon Musk, discussed her new book and Elon's future plans, including his vision of establishing a city on Mars through SpaceX.
